description: Generates ONE version of a track for an event of the Music tab (spends credits: refused until the user approved the cost in the conversation, see approve_spending). Without prompt/duration/loop, uses the event's. The prompt goes to the music model exactly as written (nothing is rewritten or added behind it), so write it in English as comma-separated tags: genre, mood, instruments, tempo, production (e.g. "medieval folk, lute, warm, 90 bpm, intimate"). A genre, voice or vocal_level you pass is written into the prompt as words (genre first, voice last). Parts, bpm, key_scale and time_signature are optional structure. Instrumental by default; with lyrics, pass them with [Verse]/[Chorus] tags, or ask the user to write them on the site. The duration must fit the user's plan: duration_sec says this account's limit, never ask for more. A track takes minutes: the tool waits up to 10 minutes and, if still generating, tells you to check later; with wait=false it only queues and returns a jobId for job_status (use it for several tracks: queue them all, the account generates one at a time). Before the FIRST track, the user must accept the rights notice on the site (the tool says so). Returns the new version (with the music page url), like generate_sounds. The game only plays chosen versions: if the event has none yet, the new one becomes chosen (auto_choose=false turns this off).

auto_choose.description: true (default): if the event has no chosen version yet, the new one becomes chosen, so the game plays it. false leaves the choice to the user.

bpm.description: Compose ("Andamento"): tempo in beats per minute (60 to 180 sound best).

duration_sec.description: Whole seconds, 10 to 240 (4 min). The user's plan may allow less: the server refuses a longer track.

event_id.description: An event in the Music tab (root folder of kind "music", its subfolders or entities).

genres.description: Musical style (the site's "Estilo musical"): ONE genre as a one-item list. Its words are written at the start of the prompt (empty = only your prompt).

instrumental.description: false = sung, with the lyrics below.

loop.description: true = the end is blended into the start, for a track the game repeats. Saved on the event.

lyrics.description: The lyrics, one line per row, parts marked with [Verse], [Chorus], [Bridge]... Only with instrumental=false.

mode.description: describe = only the prompt; compose = you also set the tempo, key and meter. Omitted: compose when bpm, key_scale, time_signature, genres or sung lyrics are sent, otherwise the track keeps its current mode.

prompt.description: How it sounds, sent to the model as is: English tags (genre, mood, instruments, tempo, production).

quality.description: draft (fast and cheap, to test the idea), good, high (the approved default), max (large model; may be unavailable). The price per minute follows the level.

time_signature.description: Compose ("Compasso"): beats per bar (2, 3 = waltz, 4 = most music, 6 = compound like 6/8).

vocal_level.description: Sung tracks: the voice behind the band (back), even (balanced, default, adds nothing) or up front (front); written at the end of the prompt.

voice.description: Sung tracks: who sings (gender), how deep (timbre) and up to 2 singing styles, written at the end of the prompt. Omitted: the model picks.

wait.description: true = waits for the track (up to 10 min). false = only puts it in the queue and answers at once with the jobId: for several tracks, queue them all with wait=false (the account generates one at a time, the rest wait their turn) and check them with job_status.

name: generate_music
title: Generate a track
